sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

rows: Repair the model using the supplied canonical terms: make coolingWaterChestVolumeAndHeightRequirementsCannotBeMet single-valued with sh:maxCount 1 so contradictory true/false values cannot satisfy either branch; validate the reported seaChestVolume rather than only recommendedChestVolume against the power/750 formula; encode the alternative as two smaller seaChestVolume values, not merely an alternative-arrangement boolean; and replace the area-pair SPARQL constraint with a unitless strainerOpenAreaRatio quantity having an inclusive lower bound of 4. Keep only one bounded SPARQL formula constraint and use SHACL Core for the ratio and cardinalities.

Use nltl:totalRelevantEnginePower, in kW, as the formula operand instead of nltl:maximumContinuousRatingPower; the verified comparison includes all relevant engine output, including required auxiliaries. Remove the unnecessary MCR requirement. Also encode the normal arrangement as existential: require at least one seaChestVolume approximately equal to totalRelevantEnginePower/750, without sh:maxCount 1 and without rejecting the ship merely because another reported chest volume differs. Retain exactly two volumes for the alternative branch and require each to be strictly smaller than the computed value. A bounded SPARQL constraint using FILTER NOT EXISTS without OPTIONAL can implement the normal-branch existential check.
